text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT P1 — autoscaler oscillation detected impacting /v1/embeddings (us-west-2). Multiple 5xx responses observed. Pager fired. Root cause unknown. Start: 04:45 UTC

alex: taking primary. quick summary: after a scheduled scale-up around 04:30 we saw rapid scale down + scale up loops. Pods killed during postStart probe, memory churn. customer-facing error rate ~3% for embeddings calls, small set of heavy requests amplified it.

priya: i'm the secondary for this shift, standing by. added quick checks to the runbook and kicked off dashboard alert pinned to this thread.

mateo: observability snapshot: CPU and memory spikes correlate w/ batch inference jobs from partner-workload. autoscaler target utilization toggling between 40% and 85% every ~90s. KV cache pressure looked normal.

lisa: did a temporary throttle on partner-workload route to reduce burstiness — reduced new surge by ~70% within 3m. :thumbsup:

alex: actions taken so far:
- throttled partner route (lisa)
- disabled aggressive scaleDown for the group (set minReplicaSeconds to 300)
- pinned model container image to previous revision (1.2.4 -> 1.2.3) to rule out new startup behavior
- alerted infra for node eviction behavior

priya: runbook links and quick commands I used: https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbooks/autoscaler-oscillation
```bash
# check recent scale events
kubectl -n inference get hpa -o yaml | yq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, events: .status.conditions}'
# tail logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-server --since=30m | grep -E "OOM|killed|postStart"
```

mateo: logs show postStart hook failing intermittently with "resource temporarily unavailable" before container fully warms. might be node-level pressure rather than container. node-exporter shows frequent reclaim activity.

alex: customer impact: mapped to 4 customers (2 enterprise) — one reported degraded embeddings in their pipeline. CS aware and sent an interim note. SLA risk low but we want to avoid regression overnight.

lisa: coverage gap: night ops has only one infra engineer on pager after 06:00 UTC. primary/secondary for next shift (06:00-14:00 UTC) — assigning priya primary, alex secondary? priya: confirm you can take primary at 06:00.

priya: yes i can take primary at 06:00. alex, i'll stay secondary for first 30m of my shift to sync. adding @mateo to the follow-up postmortem.

alex: handoff notes for priya:
- keep autoscaler scaleDown cooldown to 300s (we reverted config)
- keep partner route throttled until we validate 1h of stability
- if 5xx > 1% for >15m escalate to infra and flip node autoscaling to conservative mode (min nodes + disable autoscaler for group)
- run the healthcheck script found in runbook under "validation" before lifting throttles

mateo: suggested mitigation short-term: increase pod startup probe timeout and add a 10s init backoff on startup to avoid thundering during scale-up. I'll prepare a patch PR and test in staging.

ops-bot: Incident notes updated. Current status: mitigated (partial). Throttling and pinned image appear to have reduced error rate to ~0.6%. Continuing monitoring.

alex: next steps (action items):
- mateo: PR to add startup backoff + probe timeout (ETA 3h)
- priy a: monitor for full hour after handoff, escalate if >1% 5xx sustained
- lisa: open followup ticket with partner to discuss safer ingestion windows (assigned)
- alex: draft postmortem skeleton and attach logs + dashboard snapshot (I'll do this before EOD)

priya: noted. i'll also add a short checklist in the runbook to explicitly call out night-coverage infra gap and the conservative autoscaler emergency play.

lisa: pinging CS and attaching customer-facing note draft in #customer-success.

alex: final handoff: primary->priya at 06:00 UTC. leaving thread open for any questions. please react with :eyes: when you ack the handoff.

mateo: :eyes:
priya: :thumbsup:
lisa: :eyes:
ops-bot: This thread will be auto-closed once postmortem link is attached or after 72h of inactivity.
